scenes.title: A basket of tickets
scenes.narration: A busy museum does not write every visitor in the big book the moment they walk in. The guard drops a ticket in a basket, and once in a while someone counts the basket.

nodes.label: Visitor
nodes.step: A visitor walks in. That has to be quick: there is a queue behind them.

nodes.label: Ticket basket
nodes.step: The guard just drops a ticket in the basket. No writing, no waiting.

nodes.label: The counter
nodes.step: Every few minutes someone empties the basket and counts the tickets.

nodes.label: The big book
nodes.step: They write one line in the big book: 120 visitors. One line, not 120.

points: The basket is a waiting line of small things to count later. Adding to it is instant; counting happens in bulk.

quiz.q: Why doesn't the guard write each visitor in the big book right away?
choices: It would slow the queue at the door
Visitors don't want to be counted
quiz.why: Writing is slow; dropping a ticket is instant. The slow part is done later, in bulk.

scenes.title: How the clicks list fits in our story
scenes.narration: In Snip, the basket is a Redis list called clicks:pending, the counter is jobs/clicks.ts, and the big book is Postgres.

nodes.label: GET /Ab3x9Qz
nodes.step: A friend clicks the short link and is redirected straight away.

nodes.label: clicks:pending
nodes.step: On the way out, the redirect drops the code Ab3x9Qz at the end of the clicks list. That is all.
nodes.details: A Redis list used as a queue: new clicks are pushed on the end, the job pops them off the front. Pushing is a single in-memory operation, so the redirect never waits for it.

nodes.label: jobs/clicks.ts
nodes.step: Every 10 seconds the click job takes up to 1,000 codes off the list and counts them per link.
nodes.code:
const codes = await redis.lpop('clicks:pending', 1000)
if (codes?.length) await addClicks(countBy(codes))

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.step: It writes one UPDATE per link: clicks = clicks + 37, instead of 37 separate writes.

nodes.label: Stats page
nodes.step: The stats page reads the totals, at most a few seconds behind.

points: The clicks list is a to-do pile: redirects add to it instantly, the job clears it in batches.
If the server stops between lpop and the UPDATE, that batch of clicks is lost. Fine for stats, not for money.

quiz.q: What does the redirect do with a click?
choices: Pushes the code onto the clicks list in Redis
Sends it to the stats page
quiz.why: It only pushes onto the list, so the redirect stays instant; the job does the writing later.
